fields.meta_title: Team Survey Builder for Team Leads | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a team survey from a prompt: rate how the team works, check handoffs and meeting load, and run a launch retro. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Team Survey That Shows How Your Team Works
fields.hero_description: Build a team survey that rates how your team works together and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Team Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the table behind it from your prompt, and a later prompt changes either one before the next round.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your team

Name the areas you want rated, such as goal clarity or how decisions get made. Emergent drafts a rating and a comment question for each, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any of them.
fields.feature_2:
No score shown under five answers

Set a minimum group size, such as 5 people. The dashboard holds back any team or area score until that many have answered, and no one can work out a single teammate's rating.
fields.feature_3:
Every answer in a database you own

Each response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the team and the survey round. Put this quarter's role clarity score beside last quarter's before the team meets again.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when a score crosses your line

Pick the line yourself, such as any area averaging under 3.0. The app posts that area and its score to a Slack channel, or emails the team lead, once the survey has closed.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Teammates away from a desk answer one question per screen on a phone. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and a 6-person squad or a 600-person department runs on one build.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. Next quarter's team survey runs from the same build, with every earlier round still sitting in your tables.

fields.tab_content_1:
The team rates role clarity lowest, at 2.7

Halvard Logistics surveys its data team each quarter. The 11 people on the team rate 5 areas from 1 to 5, and 10 of 11 answered this round. Goal clarity averaged 4.3, while role clarity came last at 2.7. The team chose role clarity as the area to fix before the next round, and each score is saved with the round it came from.
fields.tab_content_2:
A 2.4 handoff score goes to #support-leads

Brightwater Health's support team hands tickets to 4 other teams and gets them back. Its 16 agents rate each handoff from 1 to 5, and any team averaging under 3.0 goes to the #support-leads channel in Slack. Engineering averaged 2.4, the only team under the line, while billing scored 3.9.
fields.tab_content_3:
Over 10 hours of meetings for 7 of 12 designers

Corvel Studio counted meeting hours before planning its next quarter. Each of its 12 designers picked a band for last week's time in meetings. Of the 12, 7 chose over 10 hours, 3 chose 5 to 10 hours, and 2 chose under 5. The team dropped its Friday status meeting and moved those updates to a written thread.
fields.tab_content_4:
After launch, 8 of 12 name late spec changes

Fenmore Robotics sent its 14-person firmware team a 3-question retro after launch, and it opened on their phones. Of the 14, 12 answered. Asked what slowed the launch most, 8 of 12 picked late spec changes and 3 picked short test hardware. The team now freezes the spec 2 weeks before each build.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Team Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a team survey that people answer honestly and that ends in one change the whole team agrees to try.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what this round is for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick four to six areas to rate
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Use one scale for every statement
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add one open question per area
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle the purpose before you write a single question. A quarterly check on how the team works, a handoff review, and a project retro need different surveys. Put that purpose in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the survey around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Rate things the team can change itself, like goal clarity, role clarity, handoffs, and how decisions get made. Leave out pay and company policy. Give each area three or four statements, and keep the whole survey near 20 statements.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Score every statement on the same 1-to-5 agree scale. One scale lets you compare areas inside a round and line up this quarter's scores with last quarter's. Label both ends in plain words, such as strongly disagree and strongly agree.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under each area, ask one open question, such as what would raise this score. A rating shows where the team is weak. The comments explain why, and they point to the change worth trying first.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell the team who sees raw comments and who sees only totals, in one sentence at the top of the survey. On a team under 10 people, report areas rather than single questions, and hold back any score with fewer than 5 answers.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give the survey a close date
fields.howto_step_6_des: Leave the survey open for one working week, with a reminder two days before it closes. Send it midweek, away from a deadline or a release. Track the response count each day, and chase only the whole team, never one person.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share results and pick one change
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share the scores and a summary of comments within two weeks of closing. Ask the team to pick the lowest area and agree on one change to try before the next round. Run the same survey again later and compare that area's score.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions to ask a team survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions to ask a team survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions to ask a team survey?

faq_plan.a: Good team survey questions ask how this team works, not how the company is run. Have people rate statements such as: I know what my role is on this project, and I can count on teammates to deliver what they commit to. Add one on safety: I can raise a problem without it being held against me. End with an open question about what the team should change first.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a team survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the areas to rate and who sees the results. Emergent builds the survey with a results dashboard, and keeps every response in a database you own. Ask for changes to any question in a later prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should a team survey template include?
faq_plan.a: A team survey template needs five parts. Open with a line that says who reads raw comments. Then come the rated areas, an open question under each, and a field for the team or role. Close on a thank-you screen that says when results come back. On Emergent, the template starts as a prompt, and editing that prompt rebuilds the survey.

faq_plan.q: What are some team survey examples for different situations?
faq_plan.a: Team survey examples include a quarterly rating of goals and roles, a review of handoffs between teams, a count of meeting hours, a launch retro, and a check-in 60 days after a reorg. Each one asks the people still on the team. When someone leaves, ask about their time on the team in an exit survey instead.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a team survey have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 15 to 20 rated statements plus one open question per area. A survey that size fits in one sitting, and people finish it instead of saving it for later. A launch retro or a check on a single handoff needs only 3 to 5 questions.

faq_plan.q: How do you keep a team survey anonymous on a small team?
faq_plan.a: Drop the demographic questions first. On a team of 7, asking for role and tenure can narrow a group down to one person. Show area averages instead of single answers, and strip names from comments before anyone reads them. Each response sits in a database you own on Emergent, not in a vendor's account.

faq_plan.q: Which topics should a team survey leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out anything the team cannot change on its own: pay, benefits, company strategy, and ratings of one named person. Those topics need a different owner and a different survey. Ask about benefits in an employee benefits survey, and keep ratings of the team lead for a separate upward review.

faq_plan.q: What should a team lead do after the team survey results come in?
faq_plan.a: Hold a 30-minute team meeting on the results. Show every area score, the lowest included, and read a few comments aloud with names removed. Let the team choose the change, write down who owns it, and open the next round's intro by saying what changed since the last one.

faq_plan.q: What does a team effectiveness survey measure?
faq_plan.a: A team effectiveness survey measures how a team works together: whether goals and roles are clear, whether people rely on each other, and whether they feel safe raising problems. Google's re:Work research found that how the team worked together mattered more than who was on it. It names five key dynamics of effective teams.

faq_plan.q: How is a team survey different from a company-wide survey?
faq_plan.a: A team survey asks one team how it works together, and its results go to that team and its lead. A company-wide survey asks every employee about the organization, and its results go to leadership. To measure shared values and norms across the company, run a culture survey, and keep the team survey for what one team can fix.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between form-tool landing pages (Microsoft Forms, SurveyMonkey's team performance template), a Gallup engagement product page and team effectiveness questionnaires from Culture Amp and a university PDF, each a fixed question list. This page is the team survey a team lead builds for one team: four surveys from a prompt, each ending in one change the team agrees to (a team effectiveness rating that finds role clarity weakest, a handoff check that flags one partner team, a meeting load count that drops a weekly meeting, a launch retro answered on phones). The FAQ covers the questions to ask, length, anonymity on a small team and what to do with results. Company-wide engagement, leader ratings and frequent short check-ins belong to the engagement, leadership and pulse siblings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Team Survey That Shows How Your Team Works'; meta title 'Team Survey Builder for Team Leads | Emergent'; hero 'Build a team survey that rates how your team works together and saves every answer to a database you own.' (104 chars, carries primary, leads with Build); how-to description one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 mixes form tools, a team performance template and team effectiveness questionnaires; page gives example questions (FAQ 1), template parts (FAQ 3), examples (FAQ 4), length, small-team anonymity, a 7-step how-to and a team effectiveness answer (FAQ 9).

specificity.evidence: Team-lead vocabulary throughout: 'goal clarity or how decisions get made', 'hands tickets to 4 other teams', 'freezes the spec 2 weeks before each build'; table rows are library-generated for survey tools.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Name the areas you want rated...', 'Set a minimum group size...', 'Corvel Studio counted meeting hours before planning its next quarter.'

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings or run-on lists; QC Q5-Q8 clean. Repeated nouns ('score' 11, 'round' 10, 'clarity' 10) kept as a note.

voice.evidence: Plain product-led sentences with concrete detail: 'The team dropped its Friday status meeting and moved those updates to a written thread.' No AI tells.

truth.evidence: re:Work claims in FAQ 9 match both domain_sources quotes ('how the team worked together mattered more than who was on it'; 'five key dynamics'); table cells for SurveyMonkey, Microsoft Forms and SurveyHero equal rules/competitors/sqb.json; tab numbers add up (2+3+7=12, 8+3+1=12, 10 of 11, 12 of 14); 5-answer threshold agrees in feature_2 and howto_step_5.

distinct.evidence: Tabs (team effectiveness, partner handoffs, meeting load, launch retro) do not overlap leadership-survey (upward feedback), pulse-survey (recurring cadence), employee-engagement-survey (census, eNPS) or manager-feedback-survey (one manager's report); FAQ 7 and 10 route benefits, leader ratings and culture to siblings.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, no brands or formats; hub link in item 2; links to exit survey, employee benefits survey, culture survey (all live); Emergent moat lines in items 3 and 6; paa gate 10/10, verbatim ok.

images.evidence: Contact sheet: one hero per tab, each matching its copy ('Role clarity: 2.7', 'Engineering: 2.4' posted to #support-leads, '7 of 12: over 10 hours', 'Late spec changes: 8 of 12'); cursor on button edges; cover and share card clean.
